forecast-period.text: A high pressure system southeast of SA continues extending a ridge across the state, as it moves over Victoria and into the Tasman Sea by late Monday. A cold front is then forecast to move across the state on Tuesday, as another ridge and high push in behind the front on Wednesday. Another cold front may slip across the southeast parts of SA early Thursday, with the high moving over eastern SA.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Morning fog and frost patches on and east of the ranges, with possible fog also about parts of the Eyre and Yorke Peninsula. Dry and mostly sunny day. Warmer, with above average maximum temperatures. North to northeasterly winds, tending east to southeasterly in the northeast.

Isolated showers developing about the Agricultural Areas during the day. Maximum temperatures above average. North to northwesterly winds, fresh and gusty about the coastal fringe and the ranges, ahead of a west to southwesterly change extending east across the state throughout the day. Winds tend south to southeasterly in the northwest from the evening, and remain northwesterly in the far northeast.

Isolated showers across the Southern Agricultural Area, mainly about windward coasts and ranges. Maximum temperatures below average, tending above average in the north. West to southwesterly winds over the Agricultural Areas, tending northwesterly from the evening. Southwest to southeasterly winds further north.

text.p: Isolated showers about parts of the Agricultural Areas. Maximum temperatures below average for central and eastern districts, tending above average in the north and west. West to northwesterly winds over the Agricultural Areas, tending east to northeasterly further north. Winds throughout shifting north to northeasterly from the evening.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Thursday: 1 to 5 mm over the Agricultural Areas, increasing 5 to 10 mm in the South East and possibly about windward coasts and ranges, where localised falls may be higher.
